chapter: Arranging, Fletcher Henderson and Lucky Millinder
title: Henderson's nickname Smack, and how Lester Young named Sir Charles
summary: Thompson explains the name Sir Charles came when three Charleses at Cafe Society got phone calls and Lester said he looked like royalty; an agent urged gimmicks.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Well, first of all let's clarify who Smack was.
A lot of people won't know. That was a nickname for Smack, you know, like my name is Sir Charles.
And before I forget it -- I told you Lester Young gave me the name of Sir Charles.

There were three Charleses working in Cafe Society where I told you we were playing. And like they had a phone in the back where the bandstand was, and the rest rooms and the dressing rooms in that area. So when they'd call for Charles one of the guys who ran the elevator's name was Charles, my name was Charles, and another Charles. Right?

So nobody knew who it was, and of course I for some reason or another got most of the calls, and so Lester Young Johnson said, 'listen, we've got to get this thing straightened out.' He said, 'listen, my man said you look like
royalty any way, you should have a name so we can identify you he said. Baby, we're going to call you Sir Charles, you know. And that's where I got the name.
Well, so getting back to -- you know --
Count Basie said I joined the royalty family, which I considered an honor.
You know. It's a gimmick, really, one of those things.

I had one booking agent tell me once in New York, the late Billy Show, when I first went there he said, Sir Charles, you've got to have gimmicks. Always carry a brief case in your hand and have a big cigar and wear a derby. He wanted me to do like Willie the Lion. I didn't think that was too original, so I thought I would stick with my music.
